div.div: دُرْبَةٌ Custom, or habit; (IAar, T, S, M, A, K;) or habituation; (T, Msb;) and boldness to engage in, or undertake, war, and any affair: (IAar, T, S, A, * Msb, * K:) and ↓ دُرَّابَةٌ , (M, TA,) with teshdeed, (TA,) on the authority of IAar, (M, TA,) but written in the K ↓ دُرَابَة , (TA,) signifies the same. (M, K, TA.) One says, مَا زِلْتُ أَعْفُو عَنْ فُلَانٍ حَتَّى ٱتَّخَذَهَا دُرْبَةً [I ceased not to forgive such a one until he took it as a habit]. (T, * S.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
